children: U.S. Federal Housing Director Bill Pulte posted on his X account on Wednesday letters from Fannie Mae
and Freddie Mac
to lenders allowing the use of VantageScore in the origination of loans.
He is set to meet Experian, Equifax, and TransUnion this week, but has also asked Fair Isaac
to provide competitive pricing for their FICO 10T product.
VantageScore is an independent joint venture company owned by Equifax (
), Experian (
), and TransUnion (
FICO is used by 90% of lenders. "Rather than competing on price, FICO has leveraged this market position to impose a pattern of extraordinary price increases," Sen. Josh Hawley
in March.
Pulte, who chairs Fannie Mae
/Freddie Mac
criticized the scoring solutions and services provider, Fair Isaac
), as a monopoly and pushed for the use of VantageScore by lenders.
"Just like I asked Vantage, I have asked FICO to provide competitive pricing to the market for their
product. It seems that FICO is not interested in offering competitive costs but instead uses various means to increase price on the American people," said Pulte in an X post today.

"In the era of AI, credit bureaus and credit scoring companies need to add real value to hold their prices much less dramatically increase their prices. Unfortunately, I see these companies more focused on pricing, which could lead some to ruin, than innovation and competition," said the FHFA director.

"We have been meeting with various credit bureaus, and this week we will be meeting with all three credit bureaus, Experian, Equifax, and TransUnion, and are focused on lowering costs while also studying using only a single credit report and bi-merge credit reporting," he said on X.
Fair Isaac
was trading 1.21% higher at $944.60 around noon on Wednesday. EFX was down 1.53% to $168.99, EXPGY was 1.64% lower at $37.23, while TRU was -1.61% to $76.40.

title: FHFA's Pulte to meet VantageScore owners this week; asks Fair Isaac for competitive pricing
